description:
WHAT THIS CASE PINS: the OPEN is refused OUTRIGHT - the CARDFILE binding cannot be resolved at all, so the backend never answers - as distinct from case09, where the backend does answer but with a response that has no two-character batch equivalent. Both land on the same status image '9000' and the same RETURN-CODE 12, and that identity is the point rather than a duplication: 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN has exactly ONE failure arm, so a dataset that is unreachable and a dataset that reports an untranslatable response must be indistinguishable in the job log. A translation that reported them differently would have invented a distinction the COBOL does not make. A REFUSAL MUST SURFACE AS A STATUS, NEVER AS AN EXCEPTION: app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:33 declares FILE STATUS IS CARDFILE-STATUS and the OPEN INPUT at :120 has no other channel - COBOL has no exception to raise here - so the refusal has to arrive as a status. :121 is two-armed, so anything but '00' takes the ELSE at :124, moves 12 into APPL-RESULT, and :126-133 finds APPL-AOK false and runs the arm at :129-132: DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE', PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. The translation therefore catches the unreachable-dataset failure and reports it as the '9' permanent-error status, carrying the original throwable out as the abend's cause; a Java program that let the exception escape where the COBOL displays and abends would lose two of the four lines the mainframe writes and would surface a stack trace that no operator's job log ever contained. WHY THE IMAGE IS '9000': 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS has two arms and this run takes the FIRST, IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9' at :162-163. :164 moves IO-STAT1 into position one of the four-character image; :165-167 zero a two-byte binary, overwrite its low-order byte with IO-STAT2 and move the result into a PIC 999 receiver; :168 DISPLAYs the literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by that image. The feedback byte is binary zero, because a translated data-access failure carries no VSAM feedback code to report and inventing one would put a number into a job log that no backend produced - so the image is '9' followed by '000'. The trailing NNNN in the expected text really is part of the COBOL literal and is not a placeholder awaiting substitution. MESSAGE ARITHMETIC: 1 start banner + 1 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' + 1 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9000' + 1 'ABENDING PROGRAM' = 4 ordered DISPLAY_LINE entries, of 38, 22, 24 and 16 characters. NO 150-character record image appears and NO end banner appears, and both absences are assertions rather than omissions: the PERFORM UNTIL at :74-81 is never entered because :72's PERFORM 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN abends first, so :78 DISPLAY CARD-RECORD - the only live display in the program, the one inside the read paragraph at :96 being a COMMENT - is never reached; and :83's close and :85's end banner sit behind 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, which does not return. RETURN-CODE is the 12 that :124 moves in. THE SEEDED FILE IS WHOLE, AND IS NEVER READ: all fifty carddata.txt rows are seeded deliberately. A refusal over a complete, valid, correctly-keyed file proves the failure is the OPEN itself rather than an artefact of an empty or malformed dataset - case02 and case16 own the empty-input shapes, and a reader who saw no record image over an empty file would learn nothing at all about :121. RECORD GEOMETRY OF THE FILE THIS RUN NEVER READS, taken mechanically from app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy (RECLN 150), one-based and cumulative so a reviewer can check this file against the copybook without running anything: CARD-NUM X(16) at 1-16, which is also the RECORD KEY at :32, CARD-ACCT-ID 9(11) at 17-27, CARD-CVV-CD 9(03) at 28-30, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME X(50) at 31-80, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) at 81-90, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 91, and FILLER X(59) at 92-150. 16+11+3+50+10+1+59 = 150 (gate G19), and the FILLER span is space-filled and never dropped (gate G21). CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE IS SPELLED EXACTLY AS THE COPYBOOK SPELLS IT, and that is implicit requirement I1: app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy:9 declares CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE, the letter after the I is absent in the source, and the name is carried unchanged here, in card.model.CardRecord and in every sibling case - the same ruling AAP I1 makes for ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE at app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy:11. It is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: FieldDiffer compares field by field, keyed by field NAME (gate G17), so a case, a model or a fixture that quietly restored the missing letter would no longer match the copybook-derived name, and the diff would then either miss a real mismatch or report a phantom one. The field name is part of the contract this migration preserves (AAP 0.8.2) and keeping it is practice B5; AAP 0.8.9 additionally forbids attaching a note that suggests a future correction, so none appears anywhere in this file. On this path the field is never even reached: it is an unvalidated ten-character string in YYYY-MM-DD shape - '2023-03-09' in the first seeded row, and a distinct value in every one of the fifty - and CBACT02C never parses, validates, compares or reformats it on ANY path, because :78 displays the raw 150-byte group item and this run does not get that far. THE NAMING DIVERGENCE (rule R1): the unit under test is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob - an Account-named class in the account package - yet CBACT02C reads the CARD file and never touches the account file. :29-33 is SELECT CARDFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO CARDFILE, ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY IS FD-CARD-NUM, over an FD of FD-CARD-NUM X(16) plus FD-CARD-DATA X(134) = 150, and :45 is COPY CVACT02Y. The name comes from the prompt and the behaviour comes from the source; the divergence is catalogued in the register at AAP 0.8.4, so a reviewer who trusts the class name authors the wrong case. NOTHING IS WRITTEN, AND ON THIS PATH NOTHING IS READ EITHER: :120 opens INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE at all, so expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty - and an empty expectation is an assertion here, because FieldDiffer reports any dataset or row a case did not pin. :31 declares ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL and :93 is a bare READ, so no keyed read and no alternate-index read occurs on any path of this program; an alternate index would be a second access path over the same data, never a second dataset (gate G45). WIRING: app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare //STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT02C and the job declares no PARM anywhere, so jobParameters is empty and there is no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one into; its single //CARDFILE DD at :25-26 is the only dataset seeded, addressed by the CARDFILE binding key that application.yml resolves at record length 150 and never by a dataset name, so no DSNAME literal appears in this file (gate G46). //SYSOUT at :27 is the program's only output, and every DISPLAY lands there in emission order, which is why these four lines are compared as an ordered sequence and not as a set. The job is driven at tasklet/step level, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). REPOSITORY STATUS SEQUENCE (gate G47): the browse open is refused and is reported as the '9' permanent-error status - and then nothing. There is no readNext '00', no readNext '10' at end of file and no endBrowse '00', because neither the read loop nor the close is reached. The ordinary run of case03 is the contrast: open '00', readNext '00' delivering the record, readNext '10', endBrowse '00'. ENCODING is US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, and no normalisation is declared, because carddata.txt rows are already the full 150 bytes CVACT02Y declares - the 36-to-50 right-pad the harness applies to cardxref has no counterpart here. DETERMINISM (practice B7): every value in this file is a literal, with no wall clock, no random seed and no derived timestamp; although the field preserved above is an expiry date, nothing here is computed from the current date. PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for each offset and width, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the step and DD contract, and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt for the seeded rows. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: AAP 0.7.6 proves that impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, the available compiler's indexed file handler disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot be made executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator plus three absent IBM copybooks, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no alternative compiler installable - and the substitution is recorded as risk R-A. A dataset that could not be reached at all, four lines out, RETURN-CODE 12.

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges an OPEN refused outright - a dataset that cannot be reached at all: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names OPEN-CARDFILE and gives it a refusal. It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the shape used to be chosen by a switch over 'case01'..'case20' in CBACT02CParityTest, so this file showed the abend lines and said nothing about the condition that produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site reads its whole input and closes cleanly, so silence here is itself a statement. The outcome is a CICS RESP rather than a FILE STATUS because CardRepository reports this program's card-file outcomes as responses and AccountBalanceReaderJob translates them - declaring a status directly would skip the translation the case exists to judge.
